mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market, which typically precedes stronger corporate earnings and economic growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when UNRATE is below 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates robust consumer demand and economic expansion, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS are rising (defined as 3-month growth > 0.5% each).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising), the increased cost of capital and reduced liquidity lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is rising (defined as 3-month increase > 0.25%).

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) reflects strong manufacturing activity and economic growth, which typically leads to higher corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when INDPRO is rising (3-month growth > 0.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A housing start rate above 1300.0 thousand units signals strong residential construction and consumer confidence, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when HOUST exceeds 1300.0.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signal a monetary tightening cycle amid rising inflation, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL are rising (3-month growth > 0.25% for FEDFUNDS and 0.5% for CPIAUCSL).

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE above 5.0%) indicates economic weakness and reduced consumer spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in > 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%.
